title: Applied ML Eval Harness and Playbooks: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Ava Chen
summary: Unified playbook that defines standards and operational procedures for the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage at Redwood Inference.
audience: ML engineers, applied ML researchers, platform engineers, solutions engineers, and SREs responsible for model onboarding and quality monitoring.
content:
## Introduction
This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation guidance: how to onboard models, author and maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, configure the eval harness, define quantization profiles, and run regression triage. The document is intended to be a single source of truth for cross-functional teams operating model serving and evaluation pipelines.

## Goals
- Ensure consistent, reproducible model evaluations across environments (dev, staging, prod).
- Prevent regressions in quality, latency, and cost when changing model variants or quantization settings.
- Provide clear triage and rollback procedures for observed degradations.
- Maintain a catalog of vetted prompt sets and benchmarks that reflect production workloads.

## Scope
Includes: eval harness configuration & CI gating, prompt-set lifecycle, onboarding checklist for new models or model versions, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage playbooks. Excludes feature research experiments (keep those in Google Drive and link back).

## Ownership and Roles
- Applied ML (owner): maintains eval harness, prompt-set catalog, and onboarding templates.
- Serving Runtime (shared): provides profiling data and latency/throughput SLI exports.
- SRE: monitors production SLOs and escalates incidents.
- Solutions Engineering / Customer Success: provides workload-specific prompt sets during onboarding.

## Eval Harness: Standards and CI Integration
- Test types to run for every model/version:
  - Unit behavioral tests (100% pass required)
  - Regression suites (weekly + on-release)
  - Latency/throughput perf-suite (match target infra)
  - Safety & toxicity checks (threshold-driven)
  - Calibration and factuality checks (sampled)

- Metrics produced by harness (canonical):
  - Generation quality: BLEU, ROUGE, exact-match, task-specific accuracy (string).
  - Embedding metrics: cosine similarity distributions, embedding drift.
  - Latency: p50/p90/p99 per sequence length bucket.
  - Token cost: avg tokens per response, tokens/sec.
  - Regression score: weighted delta across critical prompt set (see "Critical Prompt Set" below).

- CI gating rules:
  1) Behavioral tests must pass.
  2) Regression score delta <= allowed threshold (default: 0.5% relative for critical tasks).
  3) Latency p95 must not increase by >10% for primary infra target.
  4) Safety checks: any new safety violation blocks merge until triaged.

- Example CI snippet (pseudo):
  - script: |
      ./eval-harness/run_suite --model $MODEL --suite critical
      if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
      ./eval-harness/compute_regression_delta --baseline $BASE_MODEL --candidate $MODEL

## Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Catalog structure (single-line JSONL entries recommended):
  - id: unique-id
  - name: short-name
  - tags: [task, domain, priority]
  - owner: team or person
  - dataset_path: s3://... or internal catalog id
  - example_count: integer
  - critical_flag: true|false

- Prompt-set tiers:
  - Critical (customer-facing SLOs; used in gating).
  - Coverage (broad distribution across capabilities).
  - Stress (edge cases and long-tail failures).

- Authoring guidelines:
  - Include 100–1k examples depending on task.
  - Use explicit, deterministic seeds for stochastic tasks.
  - Document expected outputs and scoring function per prompt.
  - Tag any prompts that are customer-specific and require consent to use.

- Benchmark maintenance: refresh frequency: Critical sets quarterly, Coverage sets bi-annually, Stress sets annually or as issues surface.

## Model Onboarding Guide (Quick checklist)
1) Pre-onboarding: confirm model license & security (legal sign-off).
2) Resource planning: estimate GPU memory, seq length distribution, peak QPS.
3) Local validation: run eval harness on local or staging infra.
4) Performance targets (pass/fail):
   - Quality: regression delta <= 0.5% on critical set.
   - Latency: p95 <= target_ms (set per customer/infra).
   - Cost: tokens/sec and ops cost within expected range for Dedicated plan.
5) Quantization suitability: run quantization sensitivity sweep (see Quantization Profiles).
6) Security & PII scan: verify training data and outputs do not leak customer PII.
7) Rollout plan: canary traffic at 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each stage.

## Quality Guardrails
- Automated checks:
  - Failing behavioral tests prevent deployment.
  - Regression score alerts: critical delta > 0.5% auto-alerts applied-ml and SRE.
  - Safety triggers: any flagged safety case opens a P1 until triaged.

- Human-in-loop reviews:
  - For new major versions, product and applied-ml must sign off after spot-checking 200 critical examples.

- Decision matrix (simplified):
  - Minor delta in non-critical task: document and continue.
  - Major delta in critical task: block rollout and initiate regression triage.

## Quantization Profiles and Guidance
- Profiles naming: profile-{bitwidth}-{scheme}-{perf-tier} (e.g., profile-8bit-qint8-lowlatency).
- Recommended default profiles:
  - profile-16bit-fp16-balanced (baseline for production).
  - profile-8bit-quantized-cost (aggressive cost reduction; validate quality).

- Acceptance thresholds for a quantized profile vs baseline:
  - Relative regression on critical prompt set <= 1.0% (default).
  - Latency improvement >= 10% or cost/unit reduction >= 15% to justify adoption.
  - Memory reduction sufficient to enable target deployment shape.

- Quantization sensitivity sweep (example procedure):
  1) Run calibration with 1k representative samples.
  2) Generate outputs for critical and coverage sets.
  3) Compute relative deltas for accuracy, perplexity, and embedding cosine similarity.
  4) If any metric exceeds thresholds, mark profile as "requires human review".

## Regression Triage Playbook (Operational Steps)
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Regression score delta > 0.5% on Critical set -> P1 to applied-ml.
  - Embedded drift > 3 standard deviations -> P2 alert.
  - Latency p95 increase > 20% -> P1 to SRE.

- Triage flow (numbered):
  1) Acknowledge alert and assign incident owner (Applied ML on-call if model-related).
  2) Reproduce locally: run eval-harness against baseline and latest model.
  3) Check recent deploys/rollouts and config changes (quantization, kernel updates, routing).
  4) Inspect performance traces: sequence length distribution, cache hit rates, batching profiles.
  5) If regression confined to small subset (customer or route), rollback that route or apply routing policy to fallback model.
  6) If regression widespread, initiate full rollback to previous model version and open postmortem.

- Communication:
  - Notify affected stakeholders via #incidents-applied-ml and post an incident summary to the Confluence incident page within 24 hours.

## Onboarding and Rollout Example (Canary Plan)
- Canary stages: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%
- Health checks at each stage:
  - No safety violations in sampled outputs (sample size 250).
  - Regression delta on critical set < threshold.
  - Latency p95 within allowed delta.

## Monitoring and Long-term Quality
- Dashboards to maintain:
  - Per-model: critical regression score, p50/p95 latency, token cost, safety violations.
  - Per-route: traffic distribution, model variant mix, rollback count.

- Periodic evaluation cadence:
  - Daily automated smoke for high-volume models.
  - Weekly regression run for models in Dedicated/Private.
  - Quarterly comprehensive eval (includes human review).

## Appendix: Example Commands and Configs
- Eval harness run (example):
  ./eval-harness/run_suite --suite critical --model redwood-gpt-3b --output results/critical.json
- Regression compute:
  ./eval-harness/compute_regression_delta --baseline results/baseline.json --candidate results/critical.json --threshold 0.005
